Sea Battle

WebDataRocks Edition — real-time multiplayer Battleship in the browser

What is this?

Sea Battle is a two-player Battleship game where both players connect to the same server and fight over WebSocket in real time. What makes it unusual: the 10×10 game boards are rendered using WebDataRocks — a pivot table component — turned into an interactive grid through a custom overlay and CSS cell states.

There is no central game engine. Each client owns its own board. When you shoot, your opponent's browser resolves the hit, updates its state, and replies with the result. The server only relays messages between the two players.

Fleet Composition

Battleship (4-deck) × 1
Cruiser (3-deck) × 2
Destroyer (2-deck) × 3
Submarine (1-deck) × 4

Total: 10 ships · 20 cells. Hit all 20 enemy cells to win. Ships are placed randomly and cannot touch each other — even diagonally.

How to Play

  1. Open the game in two browser tabs (or share the address on the same network).
  2. Click Generate Fleet to randomize your ship positions — repeat until satisfied.
  3. Click Ready in both tabs. The game starts when both players confirm.
  4. Click any cell on the right board (enemy) to fire.
  5. A hit is marked in red and gives you another shot. A miss is marked with a yellow dot and passes the turn.
  6. When a ship is fully sunk, all surrounding water cells are automatically revealed.
  7. The first player to destroy all 20 enemy cells wins.
  8. Click Play Again to start a new round without reconnecting.

Features

Real-time multiplayer

Moves sync instantly over WebSocket — no polling, no page refreshes.

Smart fleet placement

Random generation guarantees ships never touch — including diagonals.

Sunk ship reveal

All water cells around a sunken ship are auto-marked as misses on both boards.

Disconnect handling

If the opponent leaves, you're notified instantly and can start over.

Play Again flow

Start a rematch without reloading — the WebSocket connection stays alive.

Background music

Starts on first click to comply with browser autoplay policies.

Tech Stack

LayerTechnology
Board renderingWebDataRocks (pivot table as game grid)
FrontendVanilla JavaScript — ES modules
BundlerWebpack
Real-time communicationWebSocket (ws library)
ServerNode.js http + ws
StylingCSS with custom battle grid overlay

WebSocket Protocol

  • READY Client → Server. Player declares their fleet is set and they're ready to start.
  • OPPONENT_READY Server → Client. Notifies the other player that their opponent clicked Ready.
  • start Server → Client. Begins the game and assigns each client a player ID (1 or 2).
  • SHOOT Relayed client-to-client. Fires at coordinate (x, y) on the opponent's board.
  • RESULT Relayed client-to-client. Reports hit/miss, game over flag, and sunk-ship surroundings.
  • PLAY_AGAIN Broadcast to both clients. Resets round state without disconnecting.
  • DISCONNECT Server → Client. Informs the remaining player their opponent left.
